title: Generalize, distort, delete
header_line: My analysis of one book on neuro-linguistic programming. Not a summary of the book. Not affiliated with or endorsed by the author or publisher.

lines.text: Which words do you use that leave things out?

I said that there are entire bodies of literature based on generalization, distortion and deletion; there are whole novels built on it, for example a famous novel about a man who rewrites his own life story.
A student said it is like interchanging facts and reality, and he was not sure how to explain it.
A student said: this morning I had a lot of clothes on the floor, which stressed me and made me feel unorganized, and I spent the morning cleaning up.
I said that I keep picturing some geese by a pond and do not know why, and used it to show how an image stays with us.

I said that I have friends who owe huge sums and laugh about it, while I would be sick. I said that they have a way of not letting the number run their state. This is my remark about acquaintances and is left general.

exercise.title: Five minutes
steps: Write a sentence with always or never in it.
Write the image that stays with you and what it says.

check.q: What three patterns did I name?
What did a student give as an example?
choices: Clothes on the floor causing stress

check.q: What did I say an image does?

recap: Notice the words that generalize, twist and leave out.
